name: Wahl clippers

card.summary: A leading barber-trade clipper brand that people use at home to buzz, fade and tidy hair and beards for a sharper look.

quick.overview:
Wahl is an American grooming-tools company founded in 1921 and best known for hair clippers and beard trimmers. Its clippers are common in barbershops and homes.

They help looks by letting people keep a short cut, fade or neat beard outline without regular barber visits. T Nation forum users have recommended Wahl, with one saying most barbers use it.
quick.how: Users fit guard combs to buzz the head or blend a fade, and use a smaller trimmer for lines and beards, usually starting on a longer guard. Forum posters describe cutting every two to three weeks.
quick.risks: Minimal; nicks or uneven cuts from clippers and irritation are the usual concerns. Wahl is one of several brands (forum users also name Oster and Andis).

lead: Wahl Clipper Corporation, based in Sterling, Illinois, was incorporated in 1921 after Leo J. Wahl patented an electromagnetic clipper in 1919.[1] It later introduced a vibrating-motor clipper (1924), a vacuum clipper (1965), a cordless rechargeable clipper (1966) and cordless beard trimmers (1984).[1]

Men on T Nation have recommended Wahl for self-cutting, with one writing that they use Wahl "as do most barbers", and others pairing a Wahl clipper with an Andis trimmer for fade and line-up.[2][3] Posters also describe a cheap clipper as a way to shave or buzz a thinning head.[4]

chain: Cut or fade hair and trim beard at home
angle.text: A home clipper keeps hair or beard at a chosen length and shape, including buzz cuts and fades. Some users also use clippers to shorten body hair.

paras: Leo J. Wahl patented a clipper in 1919 and bought his uncle's company stock in 1921.[1] Later milestones included the first cordless rechargeable clipper in 1966, the acquisition of Moser in 1996 and a home-haircutting line in 2006.[1]
T Nation posters recommend Wahl for self-cutting, buzz cuts and fades, and for trimming chest hair to a short length for a better appearance.[2][3][5]

timeline.event: Leo J. Wahl patents an electromagnetic clipper.[1]
